# Why Rāvaṇa belongs in your address bar

Every address bar is a choice. When you type **Rāvaṇa**, you are not typing a novelty; you are restoring a name that the early DNS, built for English typewriters, could not carry. The plain ASCII form *ravana* is a leftover of that constraint, not the name itself. This post is the long version of the restoration: where the name comes from, how the Devanagari tradition wrote it, how it is pronounced, what the myths and the material record preserve, and why its Unicode form now lives as a working domain. The claim throughout is simple — the original spelling is not decoration. It is the name.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Rāvaṇa
- **ASCII form:** ravana
- **Meaning:** "The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa"
- **Domain of influence:** Ten-Headed King, Lanka
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** रावण (Devanagari)
- **Live domain:** ravana.com

## Overview

**Rāvaṇa** (*ravana*) — Ten-Headed King, Lanka · The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa — belongs to the Sanskrit tradition, where it is catalogued under the domain "Ten-Headed King, Lanka". The name means "The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa".

**Rāvaṇa** belongs to the Sanskrit tradition, where it is associated with ten-headed king, lanka.

PuniCodex restores the name as **Rāvaṇa** and serves its temple at [ravana.com](https://punicodex.com/ravana/). The restoration preserves at least one distinctive feature — a diacritic or a distinctive letter — that the ASCII form loses, and exactly one historically valid Unicode restoration exists, which places the name in Tier 1. The plain ASCII form *ravana* survives as a modern convenience imposed by the early domain-name system; the restoration, not the fallback, is the form the project defends as philologically complete.

## The Name

The name is attested in Devanagari as **रावण**. Etymologically it means "The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa".

Sanskrit Rāvaṇa, from the causative of rū 'to roar, to cry'; the ten-headed king of Lanka.

The ASCII form *ravana* survives only because the early domain-name system could not carry diacritics; it is a technological compromise, not an ancient spelling. The Unicode restoration **Rāvaṇa** recovers the vowel length of the original directly in the address bar. The restoration preserves at least one distinctive feature — a diacritic or a distinctive letter — that the ASCII form loses, and exactly one historically valid Unicode restoration exists, which places the name in Tier 1.

The letter-by-letter transformation runs:

- **r** → **R** — Same, capitalized
- **a** → **ā** — Macron: long vowel
- **v** → **v** — Same
- **a** → **a** — Same
- **n** → **ṇ** — N with dot: retroflex n
- **a** → **a** — Same

The canonical temple for this name is served at **ravana.com**.

## The Original Script

The name is preserved in Devanagari as **रावण**.

The scholarly transliteration is *Rāvaṇa*.

The rendering proceeds step by step:

- Sanskrit Rāvaṇa is written in Devanagari as रावण
- IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent
- Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

## Pronunciation

The reconstructed pronunciation of the name is **/ravana/** — Sanskrit Reconstruction.

Phoneme by phoneme:

- **R** — Initial character of the restored form Rāvaṇa.
- **āvaṇa** — Remainder of the name, preserving the distinctive marks of the Sanskrit tradition.

For the modern speaker, the closest approximation is: 'RAVANA' — pronounce the restored form with attention to the preserved diacritics and length.

Kindred and historical forms of the name:

- **Sanskrit** — Rāvaṇa, the restored Unicode form of the name

Rāvaṇa is Tier 1 because the Sanskrit form preserves distinctive features that ASCII loses: stress, length, or special characters.

## Mythology

The stories of **Rāvaṇa** circulate within the Sanskrit corpus, where the figure embodies ten-headed king, lanka.

### Primary Attestation (Sources)

Rāvaṇa is attested in the canonical Sanskrit sources as a figure associated with ten-headed king, lanka.

### Name and Meaning (Etymology)

The name means "The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition. **Rāvaṇa** is the ten-headed king of Laṅkā and the antagonist of the *Rāmāyaṇa*. A devout śaiva and master of the Vedas, he abducts Sītā and is ultimately defeated by Rāma, the avatāra of Viṣṇu. His character is morally complex: the epic praises his learning and power even as it condemns his lust and tyranny. His ten heads traditionally represent mastery of the four Vedas and six shastras, making him a scholar-king as well as a demon.

## The Domain Name

The restored name is live as a working domain: **ravana.com**. Behind the scenes the DNS carries it in punycode form — an ASCII-compatible encoding that lets a non-ASCII name travel the global network without breaking older infrastructure. The visitor sees Rāvaṇa; the machines see the encoding. That duality is the engineering compromise on which the entire restoration rests, and it is why a name written the way its own tradition wrote it in Devanagari can now be typed into any browser on earth.

## A Closer Look at the Marks

A restored name is a small map. In **Rāvaṇa**, the journey from the ASCII fallback *ravana* to the Unicode form can be read letter by letter, and each letter tells a story. Of the 6 characters, 4 remain unchanged; they anchor the name to its modern shape. The remaining adjustments recover marks the source tradition used to distinguish this name from every other word built from the same letters.

The **r** stays as it is — Same, capitalized.

The **a** becomes **ā** — Macron: long vowel.

The **v** stays as it is — Same.

The **a** stays as it is — Same.

The **n** becomes **ṇ** — N with dot: retroflex n.

The **a** stays as it is — Same.

Together these changes are not decoration. They are the minimum set of marks needed to keep the name legible in its own tradition. Remove them and you still have a string of letters; you no longer have the name as it was written.
